@RealDexterMidnight what??  

The name "Palestine" is over 3,000 years old, originating from ancient references to the Philistines in the 12th century BCE, while the modern political State of Palestine was formally declared in 1988. The region has a deep history of human habitation and has been known by the geographic designation "Palestine" through various empire eras.Origins of the NameAncient roots: Variations of the name (like Peleset in Egyptian records or Palashtu in Assyrian texts) date back to roughly 1150 BCE, describing the coastal Philistine people.Greek and Roman usage: Writers like Herodotus used Palaistinê in the 5th century BCE to describe the wider land. The Romans officially merged Judea into the province of Syria Palaestina in 135 CE.Islamic and Ottoman eras: The Arabic equivalent Jund Filastin was used as an administrative district name starting from early Islamic caliphates.Political and National HistoryBritish Mandate (1920–1948): Following World War I, the League of Nations established British-administered Mandate Palestine as a distinct geopolitical entity.Statehood Declaration (1988): The Palestine Liberation Organization formally declared the independent State of Palestine on November 15, 1988.Modern Recognition: In 2012, the United Nations upgraded Palestine to a non-member observer state.

replies.text: @OmarAlsadi-i9d From both a biblically and historical perspective, the idea of "Israel" and its name predate that of "Palestine" by over a thousand years. God made an unconditional covenant with Abraham, promising the land of Canaan to him and to his seed through Isaac and Jacob, who was renamed to Israel.Biblical and Historical TimelinePatriarchal Promise (circa 2000 BCE): According to Genesis 17:7-8, God makes His covenant with Abraham, saying, "I will establish my covenant as an everlasting covenant between me and you and your descendants after you… the whole land of Canaan… will be your everlasting possession."Twelve Tribes and Kingdom (circa 1400 – 1000 BCE): After being freed from Egypt, the descendants of Jacob (Israelites) inhabited the land, eventually becoming a unified kingdom with kings Saul, David and Solomon, mentioned in ancient inscriptions, such as the Merneptah Stele and Tel Dan Stele.Origin of the Name "Palestine" (135 CE): The name Palestine originates from the Philistines, which was an ancient Aegean group of people, inhabiting a narrow coastal strip of the area and disappearing hundreds of years before the time of Roman Empire. The Romans used the name Syria Palaestina for the entire region from 135 CE, in order to break the connection of Jews to their land. English

“Those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated. And those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make their matters easy for them.”
According to the traditional hadith account:

Aisha: 9 years old when the marriage was consummated.

Muhammad: approximately 53 years old at that time.

Sahih Muslim 1422b — likewise reports 6 at marriage and 9 when she was taken to his house. 


The 53 figure is calculated from the traditional chronology of Muhammad's life (born around 570 CE, consummation around 623 CE), rather than being stated as an age in these hadiths.

replies.text: @Igaveuploll     It is true from both a biblically and historical perspective, the idea of "Israel" and its name predate that of "Palestine" by over a thousand years. God made an unconditional covenant with Abraham, promising the land of Canaan to him and to his seed through Isaac and Jacob, who was renamed to Israel.Biblical and Historical TimelinePatriarchal Promise (circa 2000 BCE): According to Genesis 17:7-8, God makes His covenant with Abraham, saying, "I will establish my covenant as an everlasting covenant between me and you and your descendants after you… the whole land of Canaan… will be your everlasting possession."Twelve Tribes and Kingdom (circa 1400 – 1000 BCE): After being freed from Egypt, the descendants of Jacob (Israelites) inhabited the land, eventually becoming a unified kingdom with kings Saul, David and Solomon, mentioned in ancient inscriptions, such as the Merneptah Stele and Tel Dan Stele.Origin of the Name "Palestine" (135 CE): The name Palestine originates from the Philistines, which was an ancient Aegean group of people, inhabiting a narrow coastal strip of the area and disappearing hundreds of years before the time of Roman Empire. The Romans used the name Syria Palaestina for the entire region from 135 CE, in order to break the connection of Jews to their land. It was done by Emperor Hadrian after he suppressed Bar Kokhba Jewish Revolt.
